description: Measured costs for the KBS letter (replaces the unmeasured '50x' statement).
machine: Apple M4 Pro (14 CPU cores, 20 GPU cores), 48 GB RAM, macOS 26.6, torch 2.12.0; no CUDA GPU available, so 'GPU' numbers are Apple-silicon MPS numbers

conventions.GFLOPs: 2 x MACs of convolution and matmul ops only (aten.convolution, mm, addmm, bmm, baddbmm; attention via the SDPA math backend), torch.utils.flop_counter.FlopCounterMode, one batch-1 forward at the model's protocol input size; element-wise ops, normalisation, interpolation, pooling and SUM's selective scan excluded (scan estimate listed separately)
conventions.latency: median of timed batch-1 forward passes after 3 warm-up passes (CPU: 30 runs, MSDB 20; MPS: same), float32, preprocessed input tensor already in memory (image decoding/resizing excluded); CPU with torch.set_num_threads(6); MPS timed with torch.mps.synchronize()
conventions.memory: CPU: peak process RSS sampled every 2 ms during the timed passes (includes weights); MPS: tensor allocation after loading (weights) and the maximum driver allocation seen after passes (the caching allocator keeps freed blocks, so it approximates the peak working set)
conventions.our_finalizer: our post-hoc Gaussian finalizer (scipy gaussian_filter, sigma 4, 384x384, CPU) is timed separately and also added to our latency; DeepGaze IIE/MSDB include their learned blur inside the forward pass

iie.name: DeepGaze IIE (released, 4 backbones x 30 readout components)
iie.note: IIE computes features on the image downsampled by 2 (192x192 backbone input)

msdb.name: DeepGaze MSDB (released, CLIP-RN50x64 + DINOv2-B/14, 10 scales)
msdb.params_trainable_note: msdb_adapt: saliency network 26,460 + 3 single-dataset finalizer scalars; msdb_adapt_dsp: 13
msdb.params_executed_note: CLIP-RN50x64 visual up to layer4.2.conv2 + DINOv2-B/14 up to block 10 + saliency network (msdb_costs.json); unexecuted layers are instantiated

sum.name: SUM (released, VMamba U-Net, token 2)
sum.params_trainable_note: sum_ft_head: SUM's own output head (final_up + final_conv) only
sum.note: CPU/MPS latency uses a pure-PyTorch chunked selective scan (no CUDA kernel), so it overstates SUM's latency on a GPU with the compiled kernel

training_caveat: Training wall-clock values are read from the row summaries. They were measured while other tracks shared the machine (CPU pool workers, one MPS job at a time under the shared lock), on mixed devices, so they are indicative only; ours and msdb_adapt ran on MPS with the lock, IIE folds ran on CPU or MPS under heavy CPU contention, SUM head rows on CPU.
